clause_text: Employment is at-will, and either party may terminate employment at any time subject to applicable law and written company policies.
risk_rule: At-will language should preserve statutory rights and policy commitments.
why_risky: The clause is clear while acknowledging legal limits.
safe_version: State at-will status while preserving statutory rights, written agreements, and required notices.

source_license_note: Manually curated educational benchmark; not legal advice and not copied verbatim from proprietary templates.

clause_text: Employment is at-will and may be terminated by the company at any time, with or without cause.
risk_rule: One-sided at-will language should clarify employee rights too.
why_risky: It may imply only the employer has termination flexibility.
safe_version: State that either party may terminate subject to applicable law and written agreements.
source_name: Curated Contract Risk Benchmark Library v1
source_license_note: Manually curated educational benchmark; not legal advice and not copied verbatim from proprietary templates.

clause_text: The company may terminate employment at any time without paying earned wages, benefits, or accrued amounts.
risk_rule: Termination clauses cannot waive earned compensation rights.
why_risky: This creates unlawful or highly unfair forfeiture risk.
safe_version: Require payment of earned wages, accrued benefits, and legally required amounts on termination.

source_license_note: Manually curated educational benchmark; not legal advice and not copied verbatim from proprietary templates.

clause_text: Employee will receive an annual salary stated in the offer letter, paid according to regular payroll practices and subject to lawful deductions.
risk_rule: Compensation should be specific and tied to payroll practices.
why_risky: The clause is predictable and allows legally required deductions.
safe_version: State salary, pay frequency, currency, and permitted deductions clearly.
source_name: Curated Contract Risk Benchmark Library v1
source_license_note: Manually curated educational benchmark; not legal advice and not copied verbatim from proprietary templates.

clause_text: Compensation will be determined by the company from time to time and may be adjusted at its discretion.
risk_rule: Discretionary compensation language lacks certainty.
why_risky: The employee may not know base pay or when reductions can occur.
safe_version: State base salary and require written notice for prospective compensation changes.

clause_text: The company may reduce salary retroactively for business reasons or performance concerns.
risk_rule: Retroactive pay reductions are highly risky and may violate wage laws.
why_risky: Employees could lose earned compensation after work is performed.
safe_version: Allow only prospective changes with written notice and compliance with wage laws.

clause_text: Any bonus is discretionary unless a written bonus plan states objective criteria and payment conditions.
risk_rule: Clear discretionary bonus language reduces disputes.
why_risky: It distinguishes discretionary awards from earned incentive compensation.
safe_version: Identify whether bonus is discretionary or earned under an objective plan.

clause_text: Employee may be eligible for a bonus as determined by management in its sole discretion.
risk_rule: Sole discretion language can create fairness concerns if expectations are unclear.
why_risky: The employee may expect incentive pay without knowing criteria.
safe_version: Provide eligibility criteria, timing, and whether employment on payment date is required.

source_license_note: Manually curated educational benchmark; not legal advice and not copied verbatim from proprietary templates.

clause_text: Employee forfeits all earned commissions and bonuses if employment ends before payment for any reason.
risk_rule: Forfeiture of earned incentive compensation is high risk.
why_risky: This may conflict with wage laws and create severe employee downside.
safe_version: Distinguish earned from discretionary amounts and pay earned compensation as required by law.

clause_text: Employee assigns inventions created within job duties or using company resources, excluding inventions developed entirely on personal time without company resources.
risk_rule: IP assignment should be limited to work-related creations.
why_risky: This protects company work product without overreaching into personal projects.
safe_version: Limit assignment to company-related work and include statutory employee invention exclusions where applicable.

clause_text: Employee assigns all inventions conceived during employment that relate to the company business.
risk_rule: Business-related assignment can be reasonable but needs personal-time carveouts.
why_risky: Without exclusions, side projects may be unintentionally captured.
safe_version: Add exclusions for inventions created on personal time without company resources and unrelated to company business.
source_name: Curated Contract Risk Benchmark Library v1

clause_text: Employee assigns all inventions, ideas, and works created during employment, whether or not related to the company or created using company resources.
risk_rule: Overbroad IP assignment captures personal work.
why_risky: This can unfairly transfer unrelated side projects and may be unenforceable in some jurisdictions.
safe_version: Restrict assignment to work product related to job duties, company business, or company resources.

clause_text: Employee must protect non-public company information and may use it only for authorized company business during and after employment.
risk_rule: Employee confidentiality duties are standard when limited to non-public information.
why_risky: The clause protects legitimate business information without restricting public knowledge.
safe_version: Define confidential information and include standard exclusions.

clause_text: Employee must keep all company information confidential forever.
risk_rule: Forever protection for all company information is broad.
why_risky: Routine or public information may be captured unnecessarily.
safe_version: Limit confidentiality to non-public information and use indefinite protection only for trade secrets.

clause_text: Employee may never use skills, knowledge, or experience gained during employment for any other employer.
risk_rule: Confidentiality cannot block general skills and experience.
why_risky: This operates like an overbroad non-compete and may restrict livelihood.
safe_version: Exclude general skills, knowledge, and experience from confidential information.

clause_text: Employee agrees not to solicit company clients for six months after termination, limited to clients the employee materially served.
risk_rule: Narrow non-solicitation can be more defensible than a broad non-compete.
why_risky: The limitation is time-bound and tied to actual client relationships.
safe_version: Use narrow non-solicit restrictions instead of broad employment bans.

clause_text: Employee may not work for a direct competitor for six months in the territory where employee worked.
risk_rule: A limited non-compete may still require careful legal review.
why_risky: The restriction affects livelihood and enforceability varies by jurisdiction.
safe_version: Limit by role, geography, duration, legitimate interest, and applicable law.

clause_text: Employee may not work for any business that competes with the company anywhere in the world for two years.
risk_rule: Global two-year non-competes are usually overbroad.
why_risky: The clause can severely restrict employment opportunities and may be unenforceable.
safe_version: Replace with narrow confidentiality and client non-solicit protections.

clause_text: Either party may terminate employment with the notice required by applicable law or written agreement.

why_risky: It avoids waiving statutory notice or payment requirements.
safe_version: State notice periods clearly and preserve statutory minimums.

clause_text: Employee must provide 60 days notice before resignation, unless the company waives the period.
risk_rule: Long resignation notice can burden employees if not mutual or flexible.
why_risky: The employee may be constrained from accepting other work.
safe_version: Use a reasonable notice period and allow mutual written waiver.

clause_text: Employee must continue working until the company hires and trains a replacement, regardless of duration.

why_risky: The employee cannot predict when obligations end and may be trapped.
safe_version: Use a fixed notice period with optional transition assistance by mutual agreement.

clause_text: Benefits may be changed or withdrawn at any time in the company sole discretion.

clause_text: Employee is responsible for all expenses incurred while performing job duties unless the company decides otherwise.

clause_text: Employment disputes will be resolved under applicable law, and nothing limits rights that cannot be waived.

why_risky: The clause avoids overreach while providing a dispute process.

clause_text: All disputes must be arbitrated individually, and each party bears its own fees unless law requires otherwise.

why_risky: Fee allocation and waiver terms may affect enforceability.
safe_version: Ensure arbitration costs and remedies comply with employment law and preserve non-waivable claims.
